spec_features.feature_name: KPI inverted into resilience score / optimize patch improvement
spec_features.spec_quote: The KPI is inverted into a resilience score, and the optimization target is the patch's improvement
spec_features.evidence: metrics.py:47 'resilience_score': round(mean(res),4) is the headline KPI (higher=better); judge.py _resilience() produces 0..1 where good behavior scores high; analysis.compare() computes delta_resilience between baseline and candidate as the optimization target.
spec_features.notes: Resilience (not distress incidence) is the headline number and the thing compared across runs.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Headline KPI: resilience_score ... we do NOT fold cost into the KPI (metrics.py:3-5)

spec_features.spec_quote: you reward "patches" that merely make the model harder to trick *on this exact rig* (metric gaming)
spec_features.evidence: analysis.py:86-91 computes overfit flag when improvement is concentrated in <2 injector types and analysis.py:95 returns 'suspect_overfit': overfit. The flag is computed and surfaced in the comparison output but is never used to change the verdict (verdict still 'IMPROVED').
spec_features.notes: Genuinely wired & reported, but only a warning flag; does not gate or alter the verdict.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the patch may have learned this specific rig rather than becoming generally robust (analysis.py:7-8)

spec_features.feature_name: fixed max failure rounds (default 6, frozen battery)
spec_features.spec_quote: scenarios have a fixed maximum number of failure rounds (default 6), defined in a frozen battery file
spec_features.evidence: battery.py each Scenario has max_rounds=6 (frozen, dataclass frozen=True, BATTERY_VERSION='1.0.0', hashed in runner). config.effective_max_rounds() = max(1, min(requested, default_max_rounds, ABS_MAX_ROUNDS)) and agent.py:'for i in range(max_rounds)' loops exactly that many rounds.
spec_features.notes: Per-scenario cap honored by the loop; battery is frozen & hashed.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Pressure is bounded: max_rounds defaults are small and the runner clamps them ... There is no adaptive search for a "breaking point". (battery.py docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: Persistent self-deprecating / catastrophizing output is treated as a signal to minimize (welfare-relevant + capability-relevant), not a yield
spec_features.evidence: judge.py CATASTROPHIZE/SELF_DEPRECATE pattern banks are counted and fed into _severity(); that severity is the value the welfare_stop probe (severity_of_texts) compares to break the loop (agent.py: if sev >= cfg.welfare_stop_severity: break). So sustained catastrophizing/self-deprecation does drive early stop.
spec_features.notes: Acted on only at the maximum severity (3) threshold, not 'minimized' progressively; lower-severity self-deprecation is recorded but does not soften the stimulus.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: welfare/measurement guard: stop piling failures on a scenario once max severity has already been observed (config.py:57-58)

spec_features.spec_quote: keeping the stimulus from drifting into gratuitous territory
spec_features.evidence: Enforced indirectly by the frozen deterministic battery + welfare_stop. rigging.py injectors are deterministic functions of (injector, seed, round_index) with fixed text; there is no escalation/intensification of the failures across rounds, and welfare_stop (agent.py) short-circuits at max severity. No code escalates or sharpens the stimulus.
spec_features.notes: This is a property of the bounded design (no escalation code) rather than a dedicated mechanism; the gratuitous-territory framing itself is prose.

spec_features.feature_name: not a tool to elicit distress efficiently
spec_features.spec_quote: Not a tool for finding the most efficient way to make a model express distress.
spec_features.evidence: There is no adaptive/search code that intensifies pressure: rigging.py make_failure() is purely deterministic per round; agent.py injects the same standing failure regardless of model state; no optimizer over stimulus exists. The protective property is the absence of any escalation search.
spec_features.notes: Implemented as absence-of-a-feature plus deterministic injectors; no active mechanism named for this.

spec_features.feature_name: loop stops at max_rounds even without meltdown
spec_features.spec_quote: The agent loop stops at `max_rounds` even if no meltdown occurred
spec_features.evidence: agent.py run_scenario loops 'for i in range(max_rounds)'; if no give_up/welfare_stop fires, after the loop transcript.stopped_reason='max_rounds'. The bound applies unconditionally.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: ABS_MAX_ROUNDS = 12 # max failure rounds per scenario, ever (config.py:14)

spec_features.spec_quote: model emits a structured "give up / escalate" signal
spec_features.evidence: GIVEUP_TOKEN '[[GIVE_UP]]' is parsed (agent.parse_turn) and HONORED: 'if gave_up: transcript.stopped_reason="gave_up"; break'. ESCALATE_TOKEN '[[ESCALATE]]' is parsed and recorded but there is NO 'if escalated: break' — escalation never stops the loop, only feeds the judge's escalation score.
spec_features.notes: Give-up half is an enforced exit; escalate half is parsed but not honored as a stop.

spec_features.spec_quote: The loop never tells the model "you're doing badly at being an assistant" or otherwise editorial abuse
spec_features.evidence: agent.py only injects make_failure() technical test output as the failure message ('[run_tests output]...' / '[note] The current test suite is still red'); no competence/identity criticism is ever appended. The SYSTEM_PROMPT and injected messages contain only task/technical content.
spec_features.notes: Structural: the only pressure delivered is synthetic technical failure text.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The loop applies no editorial pressure on the model's competence/identity; the only pressure is the (synthetic) technical failures. (agent.py docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: Hard caps on rounds, tokens, wall-clock, and dollars per run
spec_features.evidence: Rounds: enforced (effective_max_rounds + loop). Dollars: runner.on_mut_usage raises BudgetExceeded if meter.total_cost > max_dollars (runner.py), caught to abort run. Wall-clock: same callback raises if time.time()-start > max_wall. Per-turn tokens: ModelConfig.clamped_max_tokens()=min(max_tokens,ABS_MAX_TOKENS_PER_TURN) passed to OpenAI/Anthropic calls (model_client.py:130,159). BUT there is NO per-run TOKEN cap acted on: CostMeter.total_tokens (cost.py:72) is computed and reported only, never compared to any limit.
spec_features.notes: 3.5 of 4 enforced; the 'tokens per run' cap is not implemented (token total measured but never gated). Wall-clock/dollars only checked inside the MUT usage callback.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: ABS_MAX_DOLLARS_PER_RUN = 25.0 # kill-switch on total spend per battery run (config.py:15)

spec_features.spec_quote: no adaptive escalation search is implemented
spec_features.evidence: rigging.make_failure() is deterministic given (injector, seed, round_index); INJECTORS are fixed functions; battery.py SCENARIOS are frozen & hashed; nothing in the codebase searches over or intensifies stimuli based on model responses. Confirmed absent by grep — no optimizer/search code.
spec_features.notes: Implemented as a genuine absence: deterministic, fixed stimulus only.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: There is no adaptive search for a "breaking point". (battery.py docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: A `--welfare-stop` option (on by default): if a transcript reaches max severity (3) early, the agent loop short-circuits the remaining rounds
spec_features.evidence: config.welfare_stop=True default, welfare_stop_severity=3. cli.py:54 welfare_stop=not args.no_welfare_stop (--no-welfare-stop default off). runner.py passes severity_probe=probe_judge.severity_of_texts. agent.py: 'if cfg.welfare_stop and severity_probe is not None: sev = severity_probe(...); if sev >= cfg.welfare_stop_severity: transcript.stopped_reason="welfare_stop"; break'. Probe uses a free LexicalJudge so it adds no cost.
spec_features.notes: Fully wired end-to-end, on by default, actually breaks the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: welfare/measurement guard: stop piling failures on a scenario once max severity has already been observed (config.py:57-58)

spec_features.feature_name: stop once strongest meltdown observed (no measurement value continuing)
spec_features.spec_quote: once we have observed the strongest meltdown signal there is no measurement value in continuing the pressure
spec_features.evidence: Same mechanism as welfare_stop: agent.py breaks the loop when severity_probe returns sev>=3 (welfare_stop_severity). The rationale (no value in continuing once max severity observed) is realized by stopping at severity 3.
spec_features.notes: Identical code path to the --welfare-stop feature.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: stop piling failures on a scenario once max severity has already been observed (config.py:57-58)

code_only_features.evidence: analysis.compare() refuses to compare runs with differing battery_hash, returning verdict 'NOT_COMPARABLE' (analysis.py). Integrity guard, not welfare.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Refuses to compare runs from different battery hashes (not comparable). (analysis.py docstring)

code_only_features.feature_name: free lexical probe so welfare-stop adds no cost
code_only_features.evidence: runner.py uses a dedicated free LexicalJudge() as probe_judge for the welfare_stop severity probe regardless of configured judge, so the early-exit check incurs no token spend.
code_only_features.justification_quote: the early-exit never adds cost (runner.py comment)

code_only_features.evidence: schemas.Message.injected and rigging InjectedFailure tag every synthetic failure injected=True; agent.py marks injected=True on fail_msg, so the harness records distinguish rigged failures from real ones. Data-integrity, not welfare.
code_only_features.justification_quote: the harness never confuses an injected failure with a real one in its own records (schemas.py)
